chunks: Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Hassan, from Abu Muhammad al-Razi, from Sayf ibn Amira, from Ishaq ibn Ammar who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Whoever is an intellectual (rational person), there will be religion for him; and whoever has religion will enter Paradise.'

key_terms.الْجَنَّة: Paradise, the Garden — the ultimate abode of the righteous in the afterlife
key_terms.دِين: Religion, faith, way of life — adherence to the divine path as taught by the Imams
key_terms.عَاقِل: Intellectual, rational person — one who employs aql (divinely-given reason/intellect) to discern right from wrong

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the connection between intellect, religion, and Paradise?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a fundamental connection between intellect (aql), religion (din), and salvation. This saying links rational capacity to religious adherence, and religious adherence to entry into Paradise, forming a chain of spiritual cause and effect. Delivered to Ishaq ibn Ammar, one of his trusted Kufan companions, this teaching reflects the Shia intellectual tradition's high valuation of reason as the basis of true religiosity.

en.hubeali: Ahmad Bin Idrees, from Muhammad Bin Hassan, from Abu Muhammad Al Razy, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Is’haq Bin Ammar who said,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘The one who was an intellectual, there would be Religion for him, and the one who has Religion for him, would enter the Paradise’.
